web.title: RF-LSTM carbon price prediction based on CEEMDAN decomposition and multiscale entropy reconstruction
web.description:
In view of the increasing volatility and complexity of carbon trading markets, accurate forecasting models are essential for policy formulation and risk management. This paper proposed an RF-LSTM hybrid prediction model based on CEEMDAN decomposition and multiscale entropy reconstruction. The model incorporates a rolling decomposition–prediction framework to address the nonlinear and non-stationary characteristics of the carbon market. First, the dataset is divided, and the training set is used as the initial rolling window. Within each window, CEEMDAN decomposes the carbon price series into multiple intrinsic mode functions (IMFs). These IMFs are then grouped according to their similarity in multiscale entropy. The grouped high-frequency components are predicted using the RF model, while the remaining components are modeled by LSTM networks. The prediction results are then integrated to forecast the next data point. After each prediction step, the training window moves forward, and the entire process of decomposition, reconstruction, and prediction is repeated until the end of the series. Experiments using Hubei and European Union data demonstrate the superior accuracy and stability of the proposed model. In addition, a composite score metric, combining model error and runtime, is introduced to provide a balanced evaluation of forecasting performance.

To further enhance forecasting accuracy and reliability, this study introduces a novel Random Forest–Long Short-Term Memory (RF–LSTM) hybrid model. The model is developed based on CEEMDAN decomposition and multiscale entropy–based reconstruction to more effectively extract hidden information from carbon price data. It incorporates a rolling decomposition–prediction framework, which mitigates the issue of information leakage during the forecasting process.

This study introduces the innovative multi-scale hybrid framework of CEEMDAN-MS-RF-LSTM (CMRL) for carbon price prediction. Inspired by reference[49](/article/10.1038/s41598-026-35085-5#ref-CR49), this framework employs the rolling decomposition-prediction mechanism (Fig. [3](/article/10.1038/s41598-026-35085-5#Fig3)). This integrated design enables the model to continuously update its decomposition and prediction processes, thereby capturing the evolving dynamics of carbon price series more effectively.

To address the nonlinear, non-stationary, and multifractal nature of carbon price series, this study develops a hybrid framework (CMRL). The model integrates a rolling decomposition prediction mechanism to adaptively capture the evolving dynamics of carbon markets. Within each rolling window, CEEMDAN decomposes the carbon price data into multiple intrinsic mode functions (IMFs). These IMFs are then reconstructed based on their multiscale entropy similarity to enhance signal interpretability. RF is used to train the highest-frequency part of the reconstructed data, while LSTM is employed to model the remaining part. Through the rolling update process, the model continuously renews its decomposition and forecasting stages, effectively improving both stability and predictive precision.
